articles.title: A qué hora es el Real Madrid - Manresa: horario y dónde ver hoy en TV el partido de la Liga Endesa
articles.standfirst: Los detalles del duelo de los blancos
articles.summary: Los detalles del duelo de los blancos
articles.body: El Real Madrid afronta un nuevo compromiso en la Liga Endesa recibiendo al Manresa en un duelo clave para mantener las buenas sensaciones tras sus recientes victorias tanto en la competición doméstica como en su estreno europeo frente al Partizan. El conjunto dirigido por Pedro Martínez buscará hacer valer su profundidad de plantilla y el talento diferencial de jugadores como Theo Maledon y Timothé Luwawu-Cabarrot para imponer su ritmo desde el salto inicial. Con la exigencia de dosificar esfuerzos en un calendario muy apretado, los blancos intentarán mandar en ambos lados de la pista ante un combativo Manresa que siempre pone a prueba la intensidad de los favoritos en el campeonato liguero. Por su parte, el Manresa visita el feudo madridista con la ilusión de dar la campanada y complicarle las cosas a uno de los transatlánticos de la competición. El cuadro visitante intentará desplegar un baloncesto dinámico, apretar las líneas defensivas y aprovechar cualquier atisbo de relajación en la rotación local para buscar sus opciones de victoria en un escenario de máxima exigencia. El partido entre el Real Madrid y el Manresa, correspondiente a una nueva jornada de la Liga Endesa, se disputará este domingo 11 de octubre a partir de las 12:00 horas (horario peninsular español). El encuentro entre el conjunto madridista y la escuadra catalana se podrá seguir en directo por televisión e internet en España a través de la plataforma DAZN, concretamente en el canal DAZN Baloncesto 2. Sigue toda la actualidad de la Liga Endesa, el minuto a minuto del partido y la mejor cobertura del Real Madrid - Manresa en MARCA.com y escucha la retransmisión en directo en Radio MARCA.

articles.title: Un Real Madrid los domingos y otro entre semana
articles.standfirst: Rotaciones entre Liga Endesa y Euroliga: Shulga, Sarr, Procida y Llull son casi fijos en ACB, pero apenas han jugado en Europa
articles.summary: Rotaciones entre Liga Endesa y Euroliga: Shulga, Sarr, Procida y Llull son casi fijos en ACB, pero apenas han jugado en Europa
articles.body: Disputados los ocho primeros partidos de la temporada, se puede observar dos clases distintas entre los jugadores del Real Madrid: los que participan en la Euroliga y los que, por el momento, deben conformarse con disputar la Liga Endesa. Entre estos últimos se encuentran Max Shulga y Olivier Sarr, los dos procedentes de la G League; Gabriele Procida, que sigue, como el curso pasado, sin demasiadas oportunidades; y Sergio Llull. El capitán y Shulga no han llegado a participar en ninguno de los cuatro encuentros de Euroliga, mientras que Sarr ha jugado 4:08 minutos y Procida, 3:46. Todos ellos, como empieza a ser costumbre, tendrán oportunidad de disputar el encuentro de este domingo ante el Kids&Us Manresa, colista de la Liga Endesa, que visita el Movistar Arena. Y más con la ausencia de Gabriel Deck, parado por sus molestias en el hombro izquierdo. "Va a ser un partido intenso. Tendremos que concentrarnos, poner en práctica las indicaciones del informe de seguimiento y desarrollar nuestro juego", dijo Sarr a los medios del club sobre el choque ante el conjunto manresano. En teoría, no debería ser una gran amenaza para los blancos, pero ya sufrieron en los dos primeros encuentros: +2 ante el Unicaja y triunfo en la prórroga contra el Obra. Con una plantilla de 16 jugadores más el lesionado de larga duración Usman Garuba, las rotaciones en las convocatorias del Real Madrid van a ser habituales en los encuentros de Liga Endesa incluso sin necesidad de problemas físicos. Es el momento de dar un respiro a quienes más juegan. El ejemplo es el puesto de base. En la primera jornada, ante el Unicaja, no jugó Andrés Feliz. En la segunda, frente al Monbus Obradoiro, no jugó Facundo Campazzo. Este domingo no sería raro que el descarte fuera Theo Maledon. El base francés está siendo el gran referente del Madrid en este inicio de temporada. Ha sido el máximo anotador en los últimos tres encuentros y en cinco de los últimos seis. Sin embargo, la doble jornada de Euroliga de la próxima semana es otra invitación a darle un descanso. Los blancos viajan a Milán y después reciben al ASVEL. Esperando la adaptación de todos tanto al equipo como a las dos competiciones y el crecimiento de algunos, hasta el momento, los domingos juegan los menos habituales y entre semana, en los que Pedro Martínez tiene más confianza por ahora.

articles.title: El Barça se reencuentra con Mirotic, el crack al que echó y sigue siendo un ídolo del Palau
articles.standfirst: Emotivo regreso del hispano-montenegrino, adorado por la parroquia culé pese a su salida traumática. En sus tres retornos a Barcelona con otra camiseta ejerció de verdugo
articles.summary: Emotivo regreso del hispano-montenegrino, adorado por la parroquia culé pese a su salida traumática. En sus tres retornos a Barcelona con otra camiseta ejerció de verdugo
articles.body: El Palau Blaugrana vuelve a abrirle las puertas este domingo a uno de sus hijos pródigos. Nikola Mirotic regresa a la que fue su casa durante cuatro temporadas, esta vez con la camiseta del Valencia Basket, y lo hará rodeado de una mezcla de morbo, recuerdos y cariño. Porque su salida del Barcelona fue abrupta, dolorosa y terminó incluso en los tribunales, pero no consiguió borrar la huella que dejó en la afición culé. El ala-pívot hispano-montenegrino de 2,08 m y 35 años sigue siendo uno de los jugadores más queridos que han pasado por el Palau en los últimos años. Mirotic llegó al Barça en 2019 como una apuesta de Estado. Firmó uno de los contratos más elevados de la historia del baloncesto europeo y asumió desde el primer día el papel de gran estrella. Ganó dos Ligas y dos Copas, aunque la Euroliga, el gran objetivo, se le resistió. Su último partido con el Barcelona fue precisamente ante el Real Madrid, en el segundo encuentro de la final de la Liga de 2023. Fue MVP y se despidió del Palau formando un corazón con las manos mientras recibía una de esas ovaciones que quedan grabadas en la memoria. Un adiós que parecía imposible que fuera definitivo. Pero apenas un mes después todo había cambiado. El 20 de julio de 2023, el Barcelona anunció que rescindía unilateralmente su contrato, que tenía vigencia hasta el 30 de junio de 2025. La explicación fue económica: el plan de viabilidad obligaba al club a reducir costes en sus secciones. Mirotic, sin embargo, no entendió ni las formas ni el fondo. La ruptura acabó en los tribunales. A Mirotic le quedaban cerca de 20 millones de euros por cobrar y recurrió a la justicia. Sin embargo, nunca hubo juicio. El 18 de julio de 2024, ambas partes alcanzaron un acuerdo económico que puso fin al contencioso. Según diversos medios catalanes, el Barcelona abonó al jugador unos 14 millones de euros, frente a los aproximadamente 22 que habría cobrado de cumplir todo su contrato. Ni vencedor ni vencido ante un juez, pero sí una salida que permitió al Barça ahorrarse una importante cantidad. La historia ha tenido un curioso epílogo cada vez que Mirotic ha vuelto al Palau. Lo hizo tres veces y las tres terminó ganando. Primero con el Armani Milan, en 2023, cuando firmó 19 puntos en el triunfo italiano (86-90). Un año después repitió cifra en otra victoria del conjunto milanés (81-94). Y en 2025, ya con el AS Monaco, aportó 13 puntos en otro triunfo visitante (74-90). Y en todas ellas el público le recibió con una ovación que confirmó que su idilio seguía intacto. Ahora regresa por cuarta vez y en un escenario todavía más especial. Tras haber coqueteado con la retirada, Mirotic firmó con el Valencia, vigente campeón de Liga, convirtiéndose en uno de los grandes fichajes del verano en la ACB. Su nueva aventura le lleva de nuevo al Palau. Allí donde fue estrella, donde levantó títulos y donde fue despedido como un ídolo. Seguro que esta tarde vuelven a recibirle como tal.

articles.title: Hugo González se luce en la paliza de los Celtics a los Sixers
articles.standfirst: El español firmó 17 puntos en apenas 21 minutos de juego
articles.summary: El español firmó 17 puntos en apenas 21 minutos de juego
articles.body: Obviamente la pretemporada sirve para lo que sirve. Los habituales deben ir cogiendo ritmo y arrancando motores y los jugadores con menos minutos garantizados, ganárselos en partidos que aparentemente no cuentan, pero que pueden dar muchas pistas a los entrenadores. De hecho, si Joe Mazzulla valora lo jugado hasta ahora, habrá tomado buena nota del rendimiento de Hugo González. El español que anotó 15 puntos ante los Cavs, mejoró sus prestaciones para firmar 17 en la paliza que los Celtics propinaron a los Sixers, 144-106. La historia debería ser muy distinta en Liga regular. El mérito de Hugo fue conseguir esos 17 puntos en apenas 21 minutos y con una línea estadística formidable: 6/7 en tiros de campo, 4/4 en triples, seis rebotes y dos asistencias. Combustión instantánea. Con él en pista su equipo ganó por 19 (su aportación en el +/-). Aprovechó cada uno de los segundos que estuvo en pista. Hay que decir que de los cinco jugadores que, normalmente, comenzarán los partidos en Philadelphia, sólo estuvieron dos, Tyrese Maxey y VJ Edgecombe. Ni LeBron James ni Joel Embiid ni Jaylen Brown, para frustración de muchos aficionados de los Celtics, se vistieron siquiera. Es la otra parte de la pretemporada, dosificación de los jugadores clave. Pero sí fue una cita especial para los Celtics. Primer partido en el Garden y puesta en escena de Paul George, debutando aunque no en partido oficial, con Boston. George logró 13 puntos en 25 minutos, aunque el mejor de los locales fue Kevin Pritchard con 25 puntos, seguido por Jayson Tatum con 23 y Derrick White con 15. Para los Celtics el partido fue una fiesta en todos los sentidos, presentación y paliza incluida, además a un rival directo, pero sabedores de que los resultados de la pretemporada son tan efímeros como nada concluyentes. Aunque es verdad que en el caso de Hugo González en Boston sí pueden servir para adivinar que su estatus en los Celtics es cada vez más sólido. Mazzulla tiene el reto de minimizar al máximo el impacto de la salida de Brown y necesita de todas sus piezas importantes para lograrlo. Hugo en dos partido ya le ha dicho a su entrenador que está preparado para ser una de esas piezas. ¿Titular? Quizá no de inmediato, pero acabará jugando muchos partidos desde el inicio.

articles.title: LeBron, Giannis and the NBA's 10 Most Fascinating Players This Season
articles.summary: The NBA is a star-driven league, where talent plus storylines equal entertainment.
articles.body:
The NBA is a star-driven league, where talent plus storylines equal entertainment.

We've got our eyes on a number of players this season, especially stars in new places, high draft picks beginning their careers or future Hall of Famers continuing to build their legacies.

There's also a lot of talent coming back from an injured 2025-26 campaign, ready to make their mark on the league once again.

Now heading into the 2026-27 season, these are the NBA's 10 most fascinating players to watch.

10. Ja Morant, G, Portland Trail Blazers

Only a few years ago, Ja Morant was considered one of the best young talents in the entire NBA, someone who made two All-Star teams, an All-NBA team, was Rookie of the Year and Most Improved Player all in his first four seasons.

Since then, injuries and bad off-court decisions have caused his career to tailspin, which is why the Portland Trail Blazers were able to acquire the 27-year-old for the modest price of Jerami Grant and Kris Murray.

The Morant experience in Portland with the Trail Blazers will be fascinating to watch.

How does he fit into a backcourt with Damian Lillard? Will Morant even start in a guard-heavy rotation that also features Jrue Holiday and Scoot Henderson? Would Morant accept a bench role now that he's extension eligible?

Morant is saying all the right things for now, although he looks like an awkward fit with this current roster. Neither he nor Lillard (36 and coming off a torn Achilles) are strong defenders and first-year head coach Micah Nori is working on just a one-year guaranteed contract .

There's some real potential for things to go poorly for a Blazers team coming off a surprising playoff run last year.

All eyes will be on Morant, who still has the talent to get his career back on track.

Cooper Flagg is coming off an outstanding freshman season, winning Rookie of the Year while averaging 21.0 points, 6.7 rebounds, 4.5 assists and 1.2 steals. The only other rookie in NBA history to meet or exceed these numbers was Larry Bird in 1979-80.

Perhaps the most remarkable stat involving Flagg? He's still a teenager, with birthday No. 20 still months away.

Flagg will be fascinating to watch not just because of his incredible physical gifts but also because of what his presence could mean for the middle of the Western Conference.

The Dallas Mavericks will be trying to win after securing just 26 victories a year ago. There's a fair amount of young talent on the roster to be sure, although players like Kyrie Irving (34), P.J. Washington (28), Naji Marshall (28), Daniel Gafford (28) and Caleb Martin (31) will want to compete now.

Will Flagg start putting up 25 points per game, make his first All-Star game and lead Dallas to the playoffs, or will he resemble fellow Duke stars and No. 1 overall picks like Paolo Banchero and Zion Williamson who wow us at first before their careers begin to mellow out?

Flagg not only represents the Mavs but is also one of the future faces of Team USA, as the Maine native looks to cement himself as a superstar in this league.

8. Tyrese Haliburton, PG, Indiana Pacers

Tyrese Haliburton is officially back on a court roughly 16 months after tearing his Achilles in the 2025 NBA Finals. His return also means a return to relevancy for the Indiana Pacers, the best team in the East not that long ago.

Indiana has become the forgotten power in the Eastern Conference, especially with the New York Knicks winning the title, Philadelphia 76ers stacking All-Star forwards and Miami Heat acquiring Giannis Antetokounmpo.

If Haliburton looks like his 2024-25 self, however, the Pacers could be the No. 1 seed in a loaded East. The 26-year-old, two-time All-Star is that important.

Haliburton averaged 18.6 points, 9.2 assists and 1.4 steals in 2024-25, leading the Pacers to the Finals. The roster he returns to now is even better than that version, with Ivica Zubac taking over for Myles Turner at center. This is arguably the deepest team in the NBA as well, with players like Kelly Oubre Jr., Larry Nance Jr. and Braden Smith added this summer to an already loaded core.

Of course, Haliburton is the straw that stirs the drink. Indiana's offense jumped by 8.0 points per 100 possessions when he was on the floor two years ago (95th percentile, via Cleaning the Glass ), as the 2023-24 assist champion is one of the best playmakers in the entire NBA.

After coming just one game short of winning an NBA title, Haliburton will be hungry and motivated to return from injury and prove that both he and the Pacers are ready to be championship-worthy once again.

All No. 1 overall picks feel pressure, although AJ Dybantsa will carry a little extra weight on his shoulders this year.

Can Dybantsa prove that the Washington Wizards even made the right choice? As supremely talented as the 6'9" forward is, players like Darryn Peterson, Cameron Boozer and even Caleb Wilson were all highly touted as well. This isn't 2023 where Victor Wembanyama was the obvious, no-doubt, don't-even-think-about-it selection. Dybantsa is great, but so are others at the top of this class.

Can Dybantsa actually lead the Wizards back to relevancy? This franchise hasn't had a winning season in nearly a decade (43-39 in 2017-18), has made it out of the first round of the playoffs just five times since the 1970s and had only made the No. 1 overall selection twice since 1962 before this summer, one of which was Kwame Brown.

Having a Wizards teammate going on record to say that the team purposely tanked last season just for the chance to draft you isn't going to ease the pressure, either.

Dybantsa was phenomenal last season at BYU with 25.5 points, 6.8 rebounds and 3.7 assists per game. He's now going to start on a Washington team alongside Anthony Davis and Trae Young, players who have 14 combined All-Star trips to their name. Winning will be expected.

Can Dybantsa have a rookie season like we saw from Cooper Flagg last year, or are we setting the bar too high for the 19-year-old already?

6. LaMelo Ball, PG, Minnesota Timberwolves

On paper, LaMelo Ball is exactly what the Minnesota Timberwolves need.

The former All-Star and Rookie of the Year wasn't able to play a leading role with the Charlotte Hornets, yet could be a high-level sidekick with his scoring and playmaking now alongside Anthony Edwards.

Julius Randle never quite proved to be a No. 2 option on a championship team, and Minnesota moved on by shipping him to the Brooklyn Nets. We'll soon find out if Ball can fill that role, a gamble the Wolves were willing to make as they revamped the roster this past summer.

Edwards is singing his praises for now, although we've seen enough in six seasons of Ball to hold our breath.

Injuries have plagued Ball nearly his entire career, limiting the 6'8" point guard to an average of 50.5 games a season. For all of the scoring highlights (including an offensive swing rating in the 99th percentile the past two years), Ball has never been a good defender, an area head coach Chris Finch could grow frustrated in with his new starting floor general.

Will Ball prove that he can play winning basketball, complement another All-Star guard and be able to stay on the court, or will the Charlotte Hornets look like geniuses for trading him while Ball's value was high?

Have the stars finally aligned for Luka Dončić this season?

Now 27, Dončić is entering the prime of his career and has a Los Angeles Lakers team that's been slowly crafted around him. LeBron James is out, an upgrade at center is in and the Lakers have filled out the rest of their roster with shooting at nearly every position.

Dončić has finished as high as third place in MVP voting (2023-24 with the Dallas Mavericks), although he could be the frontrunner for the award if he leads Los Angeles to a top seed in the West.

Dončić also appears to be in the best shape of his life, looking far leaner than his days in Dallas. Austin Reaves (23.3 points, 4.7 rebounds, 5.5 assists) is back as his sidekick on four-year, $185 million contract and Walker Kessler is the type of lob-catching, rim protecting threat Dončić should love to play alongside.

The ninth-year pro is also starting to swim in some troubled waters, however, as the pressure to win a title will be felt more than ever.

Dončić could soon become one of the greatest players to never win a championship, especially with continued All-Star, All-NBA and scoring title honors. These Lakers look good on paper, but they don't look great , especially stacked up alongside the Oklahoma City Thunder or San Antonio Spurs over the next few seasons.

Dončić has been one of the NBA's best players for years now while also benefitting from low expectations with the post-Dirk Nowitzki Mavericks.

Now in L.A., all eyes will be on the 6'8" point guard.

Nikola Jokić is likely feeling the heat from players like Victor Wembanyama and Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, although the three-time MVP is still the best basketball player in the world.

The world will be watching Jokić this season not only for his on-court abilities but also due to the uncertainty following his future with the Denver Nuggets as a free agent next summer.

Jokić declining to sign an extension with the team is the right financial move if he wants to maximize his earnings, as a five-year $359.5 million max deal awaits him in 2027.

Rival fans and teams will be watching for any signs of frustration from Jokić towards the only franchise he's ever known, as the Nuggets already lost Peyton Watson, Tim Hardaway Jr., Jonas Valančiūnas and Bruce Brown this offseason.

Potential free agent drama aside, Jokić is one of the most visually pleasing players to watch given that he can pull off passes like this:

We're witnessing one of the greatest centers in NBA history at the peak of his powers, as Jokić has finished in the top-2 in MVP voting in each of the past six years. He's rattled off eight straight All-Star trips and led the NBA in both rebounding and assists last season.

Watching one of the best in the league in their prime is always a treat. Mix in a little free agency uncertainty and Jokić deservedly ranks high on this list.

Seeing Giannis Antetokounmpo in something other than a Milwaukee Bucks jersey after 13 years is going to take some getting used to.

The Miami Heat were wise to pursue the 10-time All-Star, as they desperately needed a superstar to build around. It's fair to question, however, how many elite years that Antetokounmpo has left.

Set to turn 32 in December, Antetokounmpo is now seven years removed from his last MVP campaign. He played just 36 games last season due to injury and hasn't had a healthy playoff run of more than five contests since 2022.

Given the amount of talent now residing in the East, Miami needs Antetokounmpo to still be a top MVP candidate for the next few years, showing the same superman ability he showcased in Milwaukee for the past decade. His plus-14.8 swing rating last season (99th percentile via Cleaning the Glass ) was actually a career high.

Will we get this version of Antetokounmpo? Or will his tenure resemble that of the Boston Celtics' Kevin Garnett (also 31 at the time of the trade), where the individual numbers begin to slide but the team is still successful?

Those Celtics teams had far more talent around Garnett than this Heat squad does around Antetokounmpo, meaning the future Hall of Famer may have no choice but to continue putting up gaudy scoring, rebounding and assist numbers.

Was Miami right to give up so much to acquire a star who's now past his prime, or did Milwaukee make the right move by trading their franchise player?

2. Victor Wembanyama, C, San Antonio Spurs

Victor Wembanyama is unlike any player the NBA has ever seen, putting together a wildly impressive first three seasons where his individual talents have already led to team success.

Carrying the San Antonio Spurs to the NBA Finals in Year 3 as a 22-year-old is just the beginning for Wembanyama, who's already the best defender in the league and perhaps the best we've seen in decades (or ever).

Whereas Kobe Bryant followed in the footsteps of Michael Jordan, Wembanyama has completely blazed his own trail. There's simply no player in the history of the sport that has matched Wembanyama's combination of size (7'4") and skill with his ability to dribble, pass and shoot.

What does Wembanyama's ceiling even look like?

At age 22 he's already won Defensive Player of the Year, made two All-Star teams, won Rookie of the Year, been named to first-team All-NBA and led the league in blocks per game three times.

Each year the offensive game continues to grow a little more, with Wembanyama's bag of tricks expanding a little deeper. His averages of 25.0 points, 11.5 rebounds, 3.1 assists, 3.1 blocks and 1.0 steals came in just 29.2 minutes per game, with the Spurs allowing 12.3 fewer points per 100 possessions with Wembanyama on the floor (99th percentile via Cleaning the Glass ).

Can Wembanyama lead the Spurs to a title while still on a rookie contract? Can he become just the 11th player in history to win multiple DPOYs? Is this the year the former No. 1 overall pick is considered the best player in the NBA already?

Wembanyama is already one of the most fascinating players in the NBA, and he's just getting started.

LeBron James proved to everyone this summer that we are still very much invested in his career and free agency plans, even as he enters an unprecedented season No. 24.

We can debate whether James is the greatest player of all time. It's becoming harder to deny that he's putting together the greatest career, however.

We've literally never seen a player in the history of the sport play this many seasons. The fact that James is still performing at an All-Star level now into his 40s is something we're probably not appreciating enough.

How much further can he stretch out his playing days now with the Philadelphia 76ers?

Can James really average 20-plus points per game for a 24th straight season? Or will the amount of star power around him force James to actually put up pedestrian numbers for the first time in his career? Are we prepared to see James average 18 points a game? What about 15? Less?

It's worth noting that James has made no announcement about this being the final season of his career. His two-year contract with Philly included a player option , giving him the freedom to retire, re-sign with the 76ers for up to three years or join another team.

James no longer has a no-trade clause in his contract like he did with the Los Angeles Lakers, either. If things go south, could both parties actually look to re-route the four-time MVP?

Can James actually lead the 76ers to a title for the first time in 44 years? Will his numbers stay steady or fall off a cliff? Could this be the final chapter for arguably the greatest athlete in American sports?

Over two decades since he first entered the league, James is still the most fascinating player in the entire NBA.

articles.title: WNBA Finals: Angel Reese headlines championship showdown as league seeks to draw viewers without Caitlin Clark
articles.summary: With Caitlin Clark and the Fever eliminated, Angel Reese's Atlanta Dream face the Golden State Valkyries in a huge WNBA Finals viewership test.
articles.body: The WNBA didn't get Caitlin Clark and Sophie Cunningham in the Finals, but it may have gotten the next best thing in terms of viewership hopes. Angel Reese’s Atlanta Dream face the Golden State Valkyries in a best-of-seven series beginning Oct. 17, matching a franchise seeking its first championship against an expansion team chasing a title in its second season. Both organizations also bring distinctive cultural identities. Atlanta’s players once campaigned against their own Republican co-owner, supporting Democrat Raphael Warnock. Golden State has embraced LGBTQ outreach through Pride celebrations, drag performances and community partnerships. Those histories offer another layer to a matchup with straightforward basketball questions: Can Golden State prevent Reese from creating second chances, and can Atlanta’s defense generate enough easy baskets to win the championship? The Angel Reese show CAITLIN CLARK'S LOWEST-RATED PLAYOFF GAME STILL OUTDREW EVERY NON-FEVER FIRST-ROUND BROADCAST These Finals could provide an indication of the WNBA’s current drawing power without Clark, and just how much star power Angel Reese has. Reese brings a substantial following of her own. Her Instagram account had approximately 5.3 million followers as of Oct. 10, which is the most of any WNBA player and more than one million more than Clark. Her visibility extends beyond basketball. She has a signature Reebok shoe and became the first female athlete featured in a national McDonald’s meal collaboration in 2025. Those partnerships have put her name before consumers who may not regularly watch the WNBA. Her first Finals appearance now offers an opportunity to see whether that recognition translates into viewers following her pursuit of a championship, with Clark and the Fever eliminated. There are substantial audiences to measure against. Indiana’s decisive first-round loss to Las Vegas averaged 2.25 million viewers across USA Network and CNBC. Atlanta’s semifinal opener against New York averaged 1.2 million on ABC, according to Sports Media Watch. The games aired on different networks and in different time slots, making them benchmarks rather than a direct measure of either player’s individual appeal. The league has already demonstrated that a Finals without either Clark or Reese can attract a sizable audience. Last year’s Las Vegas–Phoenix championship series averaged 1.5 million viewers across ABC and ESPN, the second-most-watched Finals on ESPN networks behind 2024. This year’s series will air across NBC, USA Network and Peacock, adding another consideration to comparisons with previous championships. One series cannot establish the league’s permanent audience ceiling. But Reese’s championship debut could help show how much of her substantial off-court following—and the broader interest surrounding the WNBA—will follow her onto its biggest stage. Both the Dream and Valkyries have histories of left-wing activism Atlanta brings a history of campaigning against a Republican co-owner, while Golden State has established prominent ties to LGBTQ advocacy. The Dream’s political activism drew national attention in 2020, when then-co-owner Republican Sen. Kelly Loeffler opposed the WNBA’s embrace of the Black Lives Matter movement. She urged the league to replace planned Black Lives Matter and "Say Her Name" warmup apparel with American flags. "The truth is, we need less — not more politics in sports," Loeffler wrote to then-Commissioner Cathy Engelbert. Dream players and others across the league responded by wearing "Vote Warnock" shirts, supporting Democrat Raphael Warnock in his challenge to Loeffler. Atlanta’s Elizabeth Williams described the effort as voluntary and driven by players. Warnock defeated Loeffler in the January 2021 runoff. AMERICANS CLASH OVER TRANSGENDER ATHLETES AS DEBATE HEATS UP: ‘JUST GETTING OUTRAGEOUS' The following month, the league approved the Dream’s sale to an ownership group comprising Larry Gottesdiener, Suzanne Abair and former Dream guard Renee Montgomery. Montgomery, who had sat out the 2020 season to focus on social justice work, remains a co-owner and vice president. The franchise’s official biography highlights her advocacy for social justice and equality in women’s sports. Those events preceded Reese’s arrival in Atlanta by several years. Golden State, which began playing in 2025, has a shorter organizational history but has made LGBTQ outreach a visible part of its identity. Its second annual Pride Game, against Atlanta on June 26, featured a surrounding celebration with drag performances, Pride merchandise and a halftime lineup featuring Sasha Colby. The franchise also announced participation in four regional Pride celebrations and sponsorship of the San Francisco International LGBTQ+ Film Festival. The Valkyries’ advocacy earned recognition from Equality California and the National Center for LGBTQ Rights, along with a Community Ally Award from the Harvey Milk LGBTQ Democratic Club. After Golden State’s victory over Atlanta that Pride Night, Gabby Williams celebrated toward a camera with the declaration, "For the gays!" Williams and Valkyries coach Natalie Nakase have also publicly supported transgender athletes participating in women’s sports. Before an Aug. 2 game, Nakase said her emphasis on inclusion extended to transgender women. "I’m all about women, little girls deserving to play, and that includes trans women," she said. Williams expressed a similar position during a May 19 media scrum, before clip resurfaced and spread widely in August. "I would welcome a trans athlete on my team or against my team, anytime," Williams told reporters. Former NBA center Enes Kanter Freedom subsequently cited Williams’ support as an inspiration for his announced bid to enter the 2027 WNBA draft. During an Aug. 14 interview with former Auburn coach Bruce Pearl, Freedom recalled seeing comments welcoming transgender teammates and opponents and deciding to pursue the opportunity himself. Freedom later confirmed to OutKick that it was Williams' comments that inspired him. "If they don’t have any problem with it, why not just go out there and take my shot?" Freedom said. Engelbert’s last Finals and the WNBA’s next chapter This championship series will also close a chapter for the WNBA’s leadership. Commissioner Cathy Engelbert announced in September that she will retire at the end of 2026, making Atlanta’s matchup with Golden State the last Finals of her tenure. Her final season began with uncertainty over whether labor negotiations would disrupt the league’s schedule. The eventual agreement delivered substantial raises for players and a seven-year deal running through 2032, giving her successor a foundation for the years ahead. Questions about officiating and player safety continued during the season. In June, Phoenix’s Alyssa Thomas received a one-game suspension after making contact with her fist to Clark’s throat. Officials did not call a foul during the play; the league imposed the punishment after reviewing it. Indiana coach Stephanie White publicly criticized the officiating afterward. Away from the court, league officials and players also confronted online harassment and a widening debate over transgender athletes in women’s sports. An August meeting of the league’s anti-hate task force addressed both subjects. The WNBA said there were no immediate eligibility matters affecting the league and pledged further discussions with teams and the players’ association. Some changes will arrive after Engelbert leaves. A centralized replay center is scheduled to launch in 2027, giving officials access to additional camera angles and assistance reviewing eligible plays. Its introduction will provide an early opportunity for the next commissioner to demonstrate progress on a recurring source of frustration. Expansion will also continue, with Cleveland beginning play in 2028, Detroit in 2029 and Philadelphia in 2030. That means more markets, more roster spots and more pressure to turn growing interest into sustained support. Against that backdrop, these Finals offer a look at the league Engelbert is leaving behind—and the task ahead: building lasting audiences for more teams and players while addressing the disputes that have accompanied the WNBA’s growth. The basketball And there will be some actual basketball being played too. Reese reached her first WNBA Finals after averaging 16.4 points and 12.1 rebounds during the regular season and winning Defensive Player of the Year. Golden State’s Kiah Stokes could make those opportunities harder to find. She helped defend A’ja Wilson during the semifinals and collected 14 rebounds in the opener. The battle near the basket will test whether Reese can establish position and create second chances against another experienced rebounder. At the other end, Gabby Williams has taken on a larger scoring role for Golden State. She enters the Finals averaging about 23 points in the playoffs, up from roughly 14 during the regular season. Atlanta must decide how much defensive attention to give her without leaving other Valkyries open. Williams has already shown she will trust those teammates. Late in the second semifinal game against Las Vegas, she passed to Veronica Burton, whose only basket of the night was a decisive 3-pointer. Tiffany Hayes added 21 points off the bench, demonstrating how Golden State can find scoring help beyond its starters. Atlanta has its own player capable of controlling a game without dominating the headlines. Jordin Canada scored 19 points and set up 11 baskets for teammates in the win that clinched the Dream’s Finals berth. Her ability to find Howard and Reese—or attack the basket herself—will be important against Golden State’s league-leading defense. Golden State won all three regular-season meetings with Atlanta. The Dream now bring additional playoff experience through DeWanna Bonner, who arrived late in the season, while Allisha Gray’s recovery from a hand injury remains a major consideration. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The central contest is straightforward: Atlanta needs Canada to create good opportunities and Reese to keep possessions alive. Golden State needs Williams to continue leading its offense while Stokes and her teammates prevent the Dream from getting repeated chances at the basket.

articles.title: El Madrid arrolla al Manresa en el show de Procida y Smith
articles.standfirst: El italiano y el estadounidense se lucen, aprovechando sus minutos
articles.summary: El italiano y el estadounidense se lucen, aprovechando sus minutos
articles.body: El Real Madrid tuvo una plácida mañana de Liga Endesa al arrollar al Kids&Us Manresa, 120-83, en un choque que llegó más que decidido al descanso (62-38) y que en realidad empezó a decantarse al final del primer acto (34-22). Por la velocidad del juego, la defensa y la capacidad de producir de muchos jugadores, Pedro Martínez acabó muy satisfecho. Pero el rival, débil y timorato, ayudó mucho desde el otro lado de la pista. El Manresa, que tiene que arrancar su motor ACB, demostró por qué llegó al Movistar Arena como colista de la Liga Endesa y sale de él incluso con peores sensaciones. En el juego coral del Madrid habría que destacar sobre todo a Gabriele Procida, en una primera parte fabulosa, y a Nick Smith Jr. Los dos pusieron el espectáculo, sobre todo el italiano con un mate sideral y un par de triples para cerrar una enorme primera parte. Procida no contaba con la confianza de Sergio Scariolo y tampoco cuenta con la de Pedro Martínez. Pero al igual que hacía el año pasado, cada vez que sale cumple con creces. Ante el Manresa fue el mejor del partido, aprovechando el tiempo que estuvo en pista. También brilló Nick Smith, más tiempo al base por las faltas rápidas de Maledon. Smith, a veces precipitado y otras algo egoísta, sigue demostrando su tremendo talento y su condición de 'killer'. Va soltándose y cada vez es menos tímido y se va viendo su potencial. El Madrid alcanzó los 62 puntos al descanso, algo que no ocurría en ACB desde 2016. Su primera parte fue demoledora ante un equipo con chispazos pero con muy poca fortaleza como para evitar el tráiler que les atropelló. Con el partido decidido, el segundo tiempo fue algo más relajado, pero aun así los blancos se fueron hasta los 120 puntos, que son su sexta mejor anotación en la era ACB igualando la cifra lograda ante el Clesa Ferrol en 1988. Hubo momentos en los que se miró la lista por si se les ocurría amenazar su mejor anotación desde 1984 (132). El partido sirvió para que, además de Procida, brillara otro de los menos habituales en las convocatorias de Pedro Martínez. Olivier Sarr, uno de los nombres que se barajan como posible salida en breve del equipo, jugó a buen nivel para liderar al equipo con 16 puntos. Procida acabó con 15, Smith con 14 y Okeke con 11. Fueron los jugadores que más aportaron en puntos, pero en realidad el Madrid funcionó como bloque y otros jugadores también destacaron como Pradilla con un 10+8. Al Manresa el partido le debería servir como ejemplo de la forma en la que no se debe afrontar un partido. Diego Ocampo tiene trabajo por delante después de tres derrotas, encajando más de 100 puntos por partido, en las tres primeras jornadas de la Liga Endesa.
